sources.title: Juha Kinnunen, Sobolev Spaces (Aalto University, 2026)
sources.locator: Ch. 1 Lemma 1.14(4)–(5), printed pp. 9–11; Lemma 1.18 through Theorem 1.25, printed pp. 14–23; Ch. 2 Example 2.39, printed p. 59; Ch. 3 Definition 3.42 and Theorem 3.43, printed pp. 84–85. Downloaded complete 168-page PDF and inspected the indicated proofs, remarks, and conventions.

contents.name: Lemma 1.14(4)–(5), weak restriction and smooth cutoff localisation
contents.support: The source proves restriction and weak Leibniz identities; the scaffold supplies the compact-support zero-extension test argument at every order.

contents.name: Lemma 1.18, properties of mollifiers, parts (1)–(4)
contents.support: Smoothness and local finite-p convergence are used; the derivative identity is proved in the preceding local lemma.

contents.name: Theorem 1.19(1), weak derivatives commute with interior mollification
Remark 1.20, direct test-function derivation of the commutation formula
Remarks 1.22(1)–(2), completion and excluded p=∞ endpoint
Remarks 1.22(3)–(4), local test-function approximation and Lp test density
contents.support: The local compact-support construction is available in the exhaustion proof; Lp test density is a k=0 consequence, not a new page claim.

contents.name: Remarks 1.24(1)–(3), closure inclusions and warning about boundary values
contents.support: The definition records closure only; boundary traces belong to the later trace page.

contents.name: Example 2.39, reflected first-order half-space extension
contents.support: The scaffold computes the correct factor 2^(1/p) for finite p; the printed source writes 2, which is only correct at p=1.

contents.name: Definition 3.42, extension domain and bounded right inverse
Theorem 3.43, whole-space Sobolev inequality transferred to extension domains

sources.title: Richard S. Laugesen, Linear Analysis and Partial Differential Equations (Illinois lecture notes, 2020)
sources.locator: Ch. 3 §§3.4–3.6, printed pp. 56–62, Proposition 3.7 through Corollary 3.13 and Exercises 3.8–3.14. Downloaded complete 158-page PDF and inspected the indicated text and proof steps.

contents.name: Proposition 3.7, local approximation and mollifier derivative formula
Exercise 3.9, dense sets of Sobolev singularities
contents.reason: The dense-singularity construction is a capacity example rather than a proof input for approximation, zero extension, or bounded domain extension here.

contents.name: Exercise 3.11, one-dimensional Hölder estimate
contents.reason: Its quantitative Hölder estimate is an embedding result assigned to the later Sobolev–Morrey inequality page, not needed to construct the extension operator.

contents.name: Exercise 3.12, zero weak gradient gives a constant
Theorem 3.8, Meyers–Serrin global smooth approximation
contents.support: Laugesen states the partition-of-unity proof route; Kinnunen gives the full summable-error argument.

contents.name: Theorem 3.9, smooth-up-to-boundary approximation
contents.support: The scaffold uses its proved C^k extension followed by whole-space mollification, with finite p; it does not depend on the source's sketched outward-translation argument.

contents.name: Definition 3.11, W0^{k,p} as a Sobolev closure
Exercise 3.13, Poincaré inequality for H0^1
contents.reason: The Poincaré inequality is assigned to the later inequality pair; the zero-extension and density claims here do not assume it.

contents.name: Exercise 3.14, weak Poisson solution
contents.reason: Existence of the weak Poisson solution needs the later coercive-form and Lax–Milgram development, beyond this approximation and extension pair.

contents.name: Theorem 3.12, C^1-domain first-order extension
contents.support: The source supplies the finite atlas, reflection, and partition route for k=1 and finite p; higher k is backed by Oh and a local moment calculation.

contents.name: Corollary 3.13, first-order p=∞ extension
contents.support: The p=∞ case is retained using direct local Sobolev bounds rather than finite-p norm density.

sources.title: Sung-Jin Oh, Lecture Notes for Math 222A (UC Berkeley, 2024)
sources.locator: §11.3, Proposition 11.13 and Remark 11.14, printed pp. 157–159. Downloaded complete 179-page PDF and inspected both steps of the extension proof and the regularity caveat.

contents.name: Proposition 11.13 Step 1, boundary atlas and chart reduction
contents.support: The scaffold proves the weak chain rule and Jacobian bounds with precisely C^k charts and bounded inverse derivatives.

contents.name: Proposition 11.13 Step 2, Vandermonde reflection moments
contents.support: The scaffold matches normal derivatives through order k−1, sufficient for W^{k,p}; the source matches through k to obtain a C^k classical extension.

contents.name: Remark 11.14, finite-order chart regularity and stronger universal operator
contents.support: The stronger universal Stein operator is mentioned only as context and is not consumed or claimed on this page.
